---
title: "Secrets files with ttr"
description: "Use scoped credentials and file-only secret transfers, with explicit unknown-write recovery."
---

`ttr secrets` transfers files through Passwords using the same server-managed
envelope encryption as mobile deployment. The server decrypts for authorized
reads; this is not a zero-knowledge store. Values and bearer tokens are never
accepted through arguments or environment variables and are never printed.

## Get credentials

A vault owner completes fresh MFA, opens **CLI and agents**, and downloads a
credential file. Owner CLI credentials are scoped to one workspace and vault and
expire with the MFA proof, within five minutes. For an agent, select existing
items and read, write or both permissions; the token expires within fifteen
minutes and its human-approved grant within twenty-four hours. Machine tokens
cannot create vaults/items, share, rotate or issue more tokens.

Set the downloaded file to owner-only permissions before using it. Browser
file downloads cannot enforce POSIX modes. The CLI refuses a credential file
that is not owned by the current user, is readable by others, or is a symlink or
hard link.

```bash
chmod 600 /private/path/ttr-passwords.json
ttr secrets list --credentials-file /private/path/ttr-passwords.json
ttr secrets put pktm-backup-gpg --from-file /private/path/passphrase \
  --credentials-file /private/path/ttr-passwords.json
ttr secrets get pktm-backup-gpg --to-file /private/path/recovered \
  --credentials-file /private/path/ttr-passwords.json
```

The output file is mode `0600`. An existing destination is refused unless
`--force` explicitly permits replacement of a regular file. Symlinks, FIFOs and
directories are refused. A machine can replace only the existing items granted
to it; first escrow uses owner credentials. The file limit is five MiB. Labels
are visible metadata; do not put a secret in its label or filename.

## Rotate and reconcile

Use freshly assured owner credentials for rotation:

```bash
ttr secrets rotate --credentials-file /private/path/ttr-passwords.json
ttr secrets reconcile --credentials-file /private/path/ttr-passwords.json
```

A lost response is **UNKNOWN**, exit status `3`. The CLI retains the original
request ID in a mode-`0600` journal beside the credential file and blocks further
writes to that vault. `reconcile` makes a fresh metadata-only status observation;
it never repeats the write. A missing receipt, expired credential, later
rejection or failed observation cannot prove the original write failed. The
journal remains until a matching committed receipt is confirmed. There is no
abandon-and-retry switch.

The browser similarly retains both grant and token request IDs before issuing
agent credentials. If either outcome is unknown, it does not issue replacement
IDs automatically. Secret strings in JavaScript and clipboard clearing remain
best effort; byte buffers are cleared when their operation ends.

## CI identity

The OIDC exchange at `/api/v1/secrets/oidc/exchange` accepts a GitHub Actions
bearer for audience `tuturuuu-passwords`. It verifies the issuer, signature,
claim times and exact configured repository, repository ID, ref, workflow and
environment. `PASSWORDS_GITHUB_POLICIES` binds those claims to a human-approved
grant and issuer, workspace and vault. There is no wildcard or caller-selected
actor. The response is a private credential-file download; consume it through a
private file, never shell interpolation, arguments, environment or workflow logs.

The mobile audience `tuturuuu-mobile-deployment` and its release flow remain
unchanged. See [activation and rollback](/build/devops/passwords-start-void) for
Worker configuration, stop fences and release gates.
